title: Why genetic diversity matters

match.reason: The bank point covers the same core idea that genetic variation helps a population survive a new disease, but its card is broader, adding selective breeding, genetic engineering and farm-specific examples that go beyond this point, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: Why genetic diversity matters
card: Genetic diversity is the variation in alleles (versions of genes) among the individuals in a population. It comes from mutation and from sexual reproduction mixing alleles.
In a diverse population, individuals differ in traits such as disease resistance or heat tolerance. These differences exist before any change happens.
If a new disease or a change in conditions arrives, some individuals may have alleles that let them survive and reproduce. They pass those alleles to their offspring.
A population with little variation is more at risk. If the disease or change harms one individual, it is likely to harm most of them, and the population could die out.
draft.remember: More variation means a better chance that some individuals survive a change.

a.q: Why is a population with high genetic diversity more likely to survive a new disease?
opts: Some individuals may already carry alleles that resist it
The disease changes to match each individual's alleles
Every individual develops resistance after being infected
Individuals with the same alleles cooperate against it
a.why: Variation exists before the disease arrives, so some individuals may carry alleles that help them survive and breed. Resistance is not gained by catching the disease, which is the tempting wrong idea.
a.clue: Think about which differences are already present before the disease arrives.

b.q: Two orchards grow the same fruit. Orchard A has trees grown from many different seeds. Orchard B has cloned trees, which are genetically identical. A new fungus arrives that kills trees lacking one particular allele. What is most likely?
opts: Some trees in A survive, but all in B face the same risk
Trees in B survive, as identical trees share resistance
Trees in A and B are equally likely to survive
Trees in A all die, as variation weakens trees
b.why: The trees in A differ, so some may carry the allele that gives resistance. The clones in B are identical, so if one lacks the allele, all do. Identical trees do not guarantee resistance, they share the same weakness or strength.
b.clue: Identical individuals respond to a threat in the same way.

a.best: Some individuals may already carry alleles that resist it

b.best: Some trees in A survive, but all in B face the same risk
